description: Offense severity from the National Survey of Crime Severity, violent and non-violent ranked separately. Ranked per square kilometre.
source_citation: Wolfgang, M., Figlio, R., Tracy, P. and Singer, S. (1985). The National Survey of Crime Severity. Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Justice, Bureau of Justice Statistics. NCJ-96017. Table 29 (national ratio scores).
notes: eb_prior_km2 is an area of citywide-average evidence added to every cell, so a cell's own figure carries weight area/(area+0.40): about 65% at resolution 8 and 21% at resolution 9, which is right since the smaller cells hold less data each. self_weight 0.6 leaves 0.4 for the mean of the ring-1 neighbours. Both are the first things to retune. Disabled once nscs_v2_percapita was promoted: scheme_version is part of the primary key of both gold.cell_safety and gold.cell_hour_safety, so leaving it enabled kept a second complete copy of the ranking and of the 24-bucket hourly layer for a comparison that had already been made. The row and its weight table stay -- nscs_v2_percapita inherits its weights from here, and re-enabling it is a one-cell CSV edit plus a `safety` rebuild when there is a reason to run safety-compare again.

description: The same severity weights, ranked per 1,000 ambient residents-and-jobs instead of per square kilometre.
source_citation: Severity: Wolfgang, M., Figlio, R., Tracy, P. and Singer, S. (1985). The National Survey of Crime Severity. NCJ-96017, Table 29. Denominator: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census population by tabulation block (TIGER/Line TABBLOCK20), and LEHD LODES v8 Workplace Area Characteristics, 2023.
notes: Identical weights to nscs_v1 -- the only thing that changes is the denominator, which is what makes safety-compare between the two a clean read on the denominator alone. eb_prior_persons 2000 is calibrated to reproduce nscs_v1's shrinkage profile: Philadelphia averages about 4,180 ambient per resolution-8 cell, so a cell carries weight exposure/(exposure+2000), about 68% at resolution 8 and 24% at resolution 9, against nscs_v1's 65% and 21%. It is also the floor that keeps a cell with almost no ambient population from dividing by zero. jobs_weight 1.0 counts a workplace and a home as equal exposure; there is no published figure for this and it is a knob, not a measurement.
